problemStatement.plain: Szemeredi's theorem says that any "dense" subset of the integers -- one that takes up a positive fraction of {1, 2, ..., N} for all large N -- must contain arithmetic progressions of every length. You cannot avoid long evenly-spaced patterns in a dense set, no matter how cleverly you construct it. This is one of the deepest and most celebrated results in all of combinatorics.
